events.title: Barak exclave's Ak-Tash–Birlishken route restriction continuing into 2018
events.scope: Ordinary direct passage by Barak residents
events.direction: Resident movement in both directions; not all nationalities or commercial categories
events.movement: Barak residents using the nearest connection to mainland Kyrgyzstan
events.exceptions: Emergency passage was agreed in 2013; authorised supplies continued during 2013–2015. Later practice is not fully reconstructed.
events.imposing_authority: Uzbek border authorities, as attributed by DCAF; bilateral authorities negotiated restoration
events.enforcement: Ordinary local passage suspended; restored operation is asserted retrospectively by the government.
events.consequences: Residents described difficult detours; research links isolation to departures from the enclave.
events.relationship: Distinct crossing from Madaniyat, Baymak, Kara-Suu and Rishtan–Sokh. Inherited restriction qualifies because sources describe persistence into 2018.
events.status_observation: Evidence is limited to the reported episode; no present-day status is inferred.
events.official_rationale: Contemporary reporting attributes the Ak-Tash restriction to absence from the agreed bilateral checkpoint roster, pending legalization; original Uzbek instruction not retrieved.
events.context: An enclave-access restriction inherited into the study window; residents could use a much longer alternative route.
events.uncertainty: Year-only onset reconciles a February 2013 emergency-only account with later 'spring 2013' wording. December 25 is an official operational assertion, not independent traveller observation. Reopening was resident-specific. Government copies and DCAF's cited Fergana account share lineage.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Unknown onset day, supply/emergency exceptions and resident-limited endpoint preclude a uniform duration.

followup_reviews.Challenge finding: The source attributes refusal to reopen to absence from an agreed checkpoint list. I_general requires a recorded interstate/inter-authority dispute, not merely a bilateral legal-authorization problem. Keep the attributed reason, leave assignments empty, and explicitly mark known reason outside taxonomy. FUQ-168 can be resolved for the known stated reason without asserting all underlying motives are known.

The generic missing-rationale issue is therefore resolved without a code.

events.title: Poipet security barricades selectively block access to the Thailand crossing
events.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
events.scope: Access to Poipet international crossing via barricades on National Road 5
events.direction: Observed outbound access from Cambodia; no blanket bidirectional closure inferred.
events.movement: Cambodian traders and residents seeking to reach the Thai market; vehicles. Tourists and casino workers initially delayed.
events.exceptions: Casino workers were allowed past the barricades toward casinos around 08:30; this does not establish their passage across the international boundary. Foreign tourists were subsequently allowed to cross the border. Other local traders and vehicles remained blocked when reported.
events.imposing_authority: Cambodian mixed security forces
events.enforcement: On-site reporting, photographs and interviews establish multiple security barricades.
events.consequences: Traders could not reach work; individual anticipated losses are not generalised.
events.record_type: Selective state blockade of international crossing access
events.relationship: Broader November 2019 informal-checkpoint restrictions are retained as a linked lead rather than assumed identical in scope.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; current status not inferred
events.official_rationale: Prevent the planned return of opposition leaders, which the government characterised as an attempted coup.
events.context: VOA reporters documented ordinary residents being stopped at approaches to the gate. Reuters separately quoted a police spokesperson claiming only alleged rebels would be stopped; this does not erase observed restrictions on ordinary traders.
events.uncertainty: Final lifting time was not recovered. The observed restrictions changed during the morning. This is a selective access blockade, not proof that all travellers or all Thai–Cambodian crossings were barred.

source_register.Closure or restriction episode: Bosnia and Herzegovina stages pandemic foreign-entry prohibitions, March–September 2020
source_register.Current reviewed timing: Formal policy: 64–65 calendar-day difference; operational continuity not established
source_register.Current rationale subcategories: Health and biosecurity: Human disease control
source_register.Historical recorded justification: Prevent and suppress coronavirus transmission.
source_register.Historical recorded context: A targeted prohibition reportedly took effect on 10 March, expanded origins on 15 March, and broadened to non-exempt foreigners by 25 March. Agricultural, business and neighbouring-nationality exceptions expanded before September.
source_register.Historical uncertainty: 10 March is the reported effective onset, with police confirmation of implementation by 11 March; 15 March is a later expansion. First refusal time/post is not established. September permission applies from 06:00 with PCR and immigration conditions. Intermediate neighbouring-nationality permission is legally dated 28 May, while Reuters reports 1 June reopening; actual intermediate timing unresolved.
source_register.Rationale phases and overlap: One current coded subtype; no assertion that all possible motives have been identified.
source_register.Original duration qualification: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. No claim of a continuous nationwide operational closure.
source_register.Current review location: Filter Follow-up review, Audit review and Unresolved queue by ID
source_register.Current record corrections:
start date: 2020-03
start precision: month
uncertainty: Initial origin-specific ban was recommended March 10 and confirmed implemented March 11; precise effective onset remains bounded to March 10–11. September 12 at 06:00 is conditional formal admission, not observed first passage. The March 24–25 to May 28 phase remains scoped to non-exempt neighbouring-country tourists.
start earliest: 2020-03-10
start latest: 2020-03-11

source_dimensions.Countries or territories: Bosnia and Herzegovina; Croatia; Serbia; Montenegro
source_dimensions.Imposing authority: Ministry of Security and Border Police of Bosnia and Herzegovina; subsequent Council of Ministers decisions
source_dimensions.Geographical scope: Foreign-entry restriction applied at land borders; aviation closures excluded as separate measures
source_dimensions.Crossing points: Bosnian international land admission posts; individual first-refusal posts not named in retrieved report
source_dimensions.Direction: Into Bosnia and Herzegovina
source_dimensions.Affected people or goods: Initially foreign arrivals from Italy, Iran, South Korea and specified Chinese areas; additional origins from 15 March; later non-exempt foreign entrants generally
source_dimensions.Exceptions: Bosnian citizens; later documented resident, medical, worker, civil-protection/military, freight-crew, home-transit and special-permit categories; agricultural and business easing.
source_dimensions.Enforcement evidence: Border Police told RSE the initial order took effect on 10 March and field offices were implementing it by 11 March. The director separately reported five refusals on 25 March after the broader phase. No independent eyewitness observation of the first refusal retrieved.
source_dimensions.Consequences evidence: Police-confirmed denied admission; no causal estimate or assumption that all annual refusals were pandemic-related.
source_dimensions.Relationship: Separate imposing authority and movement category from neighbouring-country restrictions. Reciprocal policies must not be added as extra border-wide days.
source_dimensions.Status observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026

events.title: Latvia prohibits non-exempt passenger movement at Russian and Belarusian land borders in March 2020
events.scope: External-EU land/rail and local-border-traffic crossings; internal-EU private travel excluded

events.movement: Non-exempt passengers and passenger vehicles, including Latvian citizens seeking eastern departure

events.imposing_authority: Latvian Cabinet; State Border Guard
events.enforcement: Legal movement prohibition and contemporary LSM report of midnight implementation; no independent count of refusals.
events.consequences: Eastern private travel was restricted while private travel at EU borders had different rules.

events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026

events.context: International passenger carrier services were separately suspended. This record isolates the external-land movement prohibition, not the Baltic internal-border travel bubble.

Removal of testing requirements in April 2022 alone does not settle the earlier purpose prohibition.

events.title: Slovak hauliers obstruct freight at Vyšné Nemecké–Uzhhorod, 1–4 December 2023
events.scope: Intentional throttling of freight access at one international road crossing
events.crossings: Vyšné Nemecké–Uzhhorod road crossing and its Slovak approach
events.direction: Freight access at the crossing; evidence particularly documents Slovak-side queues toward Ukraine, not identical restriction in both directions
events.movement: Ordinary commercial trucks, prominently on the route into Ukraine; not all passenger movement
events.exceptions: Four ordinary trucks per hour reportedly admitted; humanitarian and military consignments, fuel, live animals and fresh/refrigerated goods exempt. Passenger cars and buses unaffected.
events.imposing_authority: Union of Road Hauliers of Slovakia (UNAS), a non-state protest organisation
events.enforcement: Physical protest blockade reported from 15:00 Slovak local time on 1 December and observed on its second day; Ukrainian border service confirms processing restored after blockade ended on 4 December.
events.consequences: Field report describes substantial queues. The next morning’s 625 waiting trucks are a stock, not a causal estimate of trucks newly delayed by this blockade.
events.relationship: Distinct Slovak crossing and organisers from R3-EU-004 Polish carrier blockade. Do not combine separate November and 11–14 December Slovak recurrences.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026
events.official_rationale: Organisers demanded reinstatement of permits for Ukrainian hauliers, citing competition and protection of their transport market.
events.context: Separate Slovak protest alongside Polish carrier blockades. Earlier November and later December recurrences are not merged into this interval.
events.uncertainty: Partial controlled throughput continued during the blockade. The endpoint report gives 22:00 without an explicit timezone; no exact hour-duration computed. Related recurrences are separate leads.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated actual reopening for the specified category and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. Date interval applies to the partial freight obstruction only. Start reported 15:00 local; endpoint 22:00 timezone not explicit.

events.exceptions: Reverse-direction trucks and Busia flows were reported operating in the early phase.

events.enforcement: Trucks parked to seal the border approach.
events.consequences: Long queues persisted after traffic resumed; backlog is not continued closure.

events.official_rationale: Drivers opposed repeat paid COVID testing. No six-code rationale neatly describes this fee protest; Public health is context, not the blockade’s protective purpose.

events.uncertainty: Sources date onset to 1 or 3 January. Call-off and continuation reports conflict on 11 January. The endpoint is passage confirmed by 20 January, not the first reopening date.

events.direction: Initial restriction targeted Lesotho vehicles entering South Africa; retaliatory obstruction affected bridge access.
events.movement: Hawkers and other passengers, Lesotho buses/minibuses, and pedestrians in the retaliatory phase.
events.exceptions: No formal exemptions documented; the bridge-wide vehicle blockade was removed by police.
events.imposing_authority: Manyatseng taxi operators and retaliating Lesotho transport operators

events.context: Dispute over transporting hawkers to Durban produced changing restrictions and retaliatory obstruction.
events.uncertainty: A 15 September witness traces being stranded to Sunday night, but the wider first onset is unclear. Smooth crossings on Sunday 21 September followed an 18 September arrangement; first reopening and full normalization are not established.

events.title: Kasumbalesa trucker obstruction and broader crossing closure in autumn 2022
events.scope: Kasumbalesa crossing, changing from northbound freight disruption to broader trader obstruction
events.direction: Varied by phase; both directions operating again in 6 October field accounts.
events.movement: Northbound heavy vehicles initially; Congolese small traders and wider crossing movements during escalation.
events.exceptions: Southbound traffic reportedly continued during the initial truck refusal; later scope broadened.
events.imposing_authority: Protesting truck drivers; Zambian police also closed the crossing during 5 October disturbances
events.enforcement: Driver obstruction and stone throwing, followed by police intervention and gate closure.
events.consequences: Freight queues and interrupted cross-border commerce.
events.record_type: Mixed non-state blockade and state closure
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no present closure is inferred.
events.official_rationale: Drivers sought safety guarantees on DRC routes; police intervention followed disorder. Reported killings were disputed by official inquiries.

events.uncertainty: First coercive onset is unknown: closure was reported by 3 October, while broader interruption is documented on 5 October. One archive dates resumption to 5 October; stronger operational accounts confirm passage on 6 October. Stable complete normalization is unproved.

events.title: Bonfim traders’ interrupted freight blockade over access to Lethem, September 2021
events.scope: Brazilian approach and fiscal-post gate near the Takutu/Tacutu bridge; obstruction of supply trucks bound for Lethem
events.direction: Brazil to Guyana freight movement obstructed.
events.movement: Goods trucks travelling from Brazil to Lethem, including essential supplies.
events.exceptions: Goods could reach Lethem by alternative routes. No claim that all border movement stopped.
events.imposing_authority: Bonfim residents, traders, taxi drivers and truckers
events.enforcement: Protesters blocked the highway approach and fiscal-post gate.
events.consequences: Delayed supplies; alternative deliveries mitigated reported shortages.
events.relationship: Promotes R4-AM-L004. Distinct non-state obstruction of permitted freight during the national COVID regime R4-AM-003; not a second count of that entry policy.
events.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
events.official_rationale: Protesters demanded reciprocal access to work and trade in Lethem, alleging unequal treatment under pandemic travel restrictions.
events.context: Guyana’s underlying travel regime allowed weekly goods deliveries. Protesters obstructed that permitted trade; talks on personal travel subsequently eased the dispute.
events.uncertainty: The initial action stopped and restarted on September 15. News Room reported goods arriving again before September 29, while Stabroek confirmed the protest ended by October 2. The precise final removal date and permitted movements during the resumed blockade remain unresolved.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. First action September 9; stopped and restarted September 15. Protest reported ended by October 2; exact final endpoint left null. No continuous interval.

events.title: Rumichaca phased commercial protest blockade against tariff dispute, March 2026
events.scope: Rumichaca bridge and its road approaches; passenger and freight vehicles principally obstructed
events.direction: Vehicle movement between Colombia and Ecuador obstructed.
events.movement: Freight trucks, ordinary cars and passenger vehicles on the bridge route.
events.exceptions: Pedestrians and motorcycles could cross during at least the March 11 phase; pedestrian travel also documented March 18.
events.imposing_authority: Border commerce, customs-logistics and transport worker groups, initially on the Colombian side and later on both sides
events.enforcement: Workers used trucks, other vehicles and wooden platforms on bridge approaches; structures removed at reopening.
events.consequences: Reduced customs activity and interrupted freight and passenger transport; unverified loss totals excluded.
events.relationship: Promotes R4-AM-L005. Separate from AM046 March 7 election measure, R4-AM-005 Ecuador selected-crossing regime, and R4-AM-002 February 2025 indigenous blockade. Initial brief actions and subsequent phases kept together as one protest family.
events.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
events.official_rationale: Protesters demanded removal of reciprocal tariffs and other restrictions they said damaged cross-border work and commerce.
events.context: This non-state protest followed the governments’ tariff dispute; it is distinct from the preceding Colombian election closure and Ecuador’s selected-crossing policy.
events.uncertainty: The often-repeated nineteen days is an inclusive protest-period description, not verified uninterrupted closure. Onset-day short actions and later restarts are explicit; Colombian and Ecuadorian sides joined at different times. Full daily exceptions are unknown.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Protest phases March 9–27; actual reopening March 27. Pauses, changing vehicle access and pedestrian/motorcycle exceptions rule out a continuous nineteen-day interval.

events.title: Slovak hauliers renew inbound freight blockade at Vyšné Nemecké in December 2023
events.scope: Intentional obstruction of inbound commercial freight at one road crossing
events.direction: Ukraine to Slovakia
events.movement: Trucks travelling from Ukraine into Slovakia
events.exceptions: Passenger movement and trucks travelling from Slovakia into Ukraine were not blocked by this action.
events.imposing_authority: Union of Road Hauliers of Slovakia (UNAS), non-state protesters
events.enforcement: Protesters placed vehicles across the inbound truck route; police and UNAS confirmed the renewed obstruction.
events.consequences: Freight backlog and restricted throughput; no independent loss estimate entered.
events.relationship: Separate recurrence from R4-EU-006 (1–4 December 2023), with an intervening cessation. Promotes the December portion of R4-EU-L005; November remains unresolved.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026
events.official_rationale: UNAS demanded reinstatement of transport permits for Ukrainian hauliers, alleging unfair competition.
events.context: Renewed action after the separately documented 1–4 December blockade. Limited truck passage resumed before protesters ended the action.
events.uncertainty: 13 December endpoint is first documented partial resumption at 19:30, not full removal. UNAS ended its blockade on 14 December at 21:00. Times are retained as reported without assuming matching time zones.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No computed duration: endpoint captures limited passage while obstruction continued until the following day.

Only trucks from Ukraine into Slovakia at Vyšné Nemecké; other traffic exempt.

events.title: Tanzanian restrictions on Kenyan truckers during May 2020 COVID border dispute
events.scope: Selective Tanzanian entry prohibition affecting Kenyan drivers/trucks, with implementation reported at multiple Kenya-facing posts.
events.crossings: Lunga Lunga/Horohoro and Taveta/Holili; retrospective KNA account also names Namanga and Isebania.
events.direction: Kenya into Tanzania for affected drivers/vehicles; outward goods could continue through transfer arrangements.
events.movement: Kenyan truck drivers and affected Kenyan-registered cargo vehicles entering Tanzania; goods transfer and some non-Kenyan-driven transit remained possible.
events.exceptions: Capital FM reports third-country transit permitted if vehicles were not driven by Kenyans; Tanzania-to-Kenya goods could be transferred at the border.
events.imposing_authority: Tanzanian regional authorities, including Tanga Regional Commissioner Martine Shidela; later bilateral transport-minister agreement.
events.enforcement: Regional directive and reported actual truck refusals; not a demonstrated nationwide all-freight ban.
events.consequences: Affected trucks refused entry; broader trade-value estimates not adopted as losses.
events.relationship: Promotes the existing unnumbered lead “Tanzanian retaliatory blockage of Kenyan cargo in May2020”. Related to H08, but distinct Tanzanian authority, direction and cargo/driver category; Kenya’s passenger closure was not ended by this agreement.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no inference of status at the 2026-10-21 cutoff.
events.official_rationale: Tanga commissioner cited preventing COVID importation. Reporting also attributes the restriction to perceived hostile treatment and Kenya’s passenger/testing measures.
events.context: Kenya’s May 16 passenger closure exempted cargo but required testing; Tanzanian regional authorities then imposed additional selective cargo-driver restrictions.
events.uncertainty: Contemporary reporting places a Holili/Taveta restriction on Sunday May 17; the separate Tanga/Horohoro directive began May 18. No synchronized onset at every post is established. May 22 is a formal bilateral framework, not observed complete restoration; local driver and registration criteria varied.

historical.duration_note: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. No operational interval: selective enforcement and agreement endpoint; actual full resumption not established.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Tanga commissioner directive excludes Kenyan truck drivers; later Kenyan agency account confirms dispute and selective restrictions.
May 18 is specifically the Monday Tanga directive in May 19 reporting; no synchronized onset across every crossing established.
May 22 bilateral agreement creates mutual testing and movement framework; no universal operational resumption observed.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Kenyan drivers, transfer of goods at border and third-country transit with non-Kenyan drivers distinguished; not all freight.
Varying local criteria and agreement endpoint do not support one exact uninterrupted interval.

continuity: No evidence establishes uninterrupted enforcement between the dated observations or actual lifting of an announced order.

events.title: Gabon COVID land-passenger restrictions beginning with northern closure in March 2020
events.scope: Initial northern land frontier restrictions, extended to national land boundaries; permitted movement categories changed over time.
events.crossings: Kyé-Ossi/Meyo-Kyé specifically documented; national extension covers other land crossings without separate gate observations.
events.direction: Entry and exit restrictions, with specified conditional exceptions; no uniform total two-way seal inferred.
events.movement: Ordinary non-exempt land passengers; later explicit conditional return/institutional travel and essential-goods exceptions.
events.exceptions: February 1, 2021 notice permits specified Gabonese/regional return travel and international/subregional personnel under conditions, essential food/fuel/gas/medical supplies, and authorised entry/exit with tests and special permits. Some local pedestrian passage was observed in the initial northern phase.
events.imposing_authority: Gabon Ministry of Interior and national government.
events.enforcement: Ministerial closure directives; northern bridge reportage describes enforced vehicle/traveller restrictions and limited local passage.
events.consequences: Northern travellers and transporters reported disruption; national economic losses not inferred.
events.relationship: Promotes SCL01 with stronger onset, exception and continuation evidence, while leaving the reopening question unresolved. Distinct from SC04 August 2023 coup closure and R5-AES-006 election order.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no inference of status at the 2026-10-21 cutoff.
events.official_rationale: Prevent COVID-19 importation and spread; later renewed precautions associated with rising infections.
events.context: Northern restrictions followed cases in Cameroon. National directive was reported by March 14 and confirmed March 20; June air reopening expressly left land borders closed.
events.uncertainty: Staged onset: March 6 northern restriction and national expansion by March 14, confirmed March 20. February 2021 article’s April onset is inconsistent and rejected. Later general COVID-lifting announcements/decrees do not by themselves establish land-specific operational reopening. No uniform continuous interval reconstructed.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No duration: staged onset, changing exceptions and unknown land-specific endpoint. February 1, 2021 is a dated restriction notice, not extension to cutoff.

events.title: Mali COVID land-passenger closure, March to July 2020 formal reopening
events.scope: National land-border passenger closure with freight exception
events.crossings: All national land frontiers in the policy; individual posts not exhaustively observed
events.direction: National land restriction; implementation and individual exceptions by direction not comprehensively documented.
events.movement: Ordinary passenger entry and exit through land borders.
events.exceptions: Freight and goods transport, especially essential supplies, explicitly exempt.
events.imposing_authority: President and government of Mali
events.enforcement: Security ministry instructed forces to ensure closure; no claim of observation at every post.
events.consequences: Passenger access curtailed; no quantified border-specific impact adopted.
events.relationship: Precedes and is distinct from the August 2020 coup and ECOWAS restrictions W-009/W-010, and the 2022 sanctions W-011. Neighbour-imposed health restrictions may have continued beyond Mali’s repeal.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
events.official_rationale: Containment of COVID-19 after the first confirmed cases.
events.context: Presidential address on 25 March announced the restriction; a 26 March security instruction ordered enforcement. A July decree separated land reopening from earlier air reopening.
events.uncertainty: 26 March onset is corroborated by AFP retrospective and contemporary enforcement instruction; exact first enforcement hour at land posts is not separately observed. July 31 is decree permission with health conditions, not a measured universal traffic restart.

historical.duration_note: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. 26 March to 31 July is a policy chronology; no operational continuous duration calculated.

events.title: Kyrgyzstan China-frontier COVID closure order and phased cargo restoration
events.scope: Land frontier with China; Torugart and Irkeshtam
events.direction: Both directions, with nationality/category exceptions
events.movement: China-frontier travellers and road freight, subject to exceptions and staged restoration
events.exceptions: February 3 summary includes diplomats, returning citizens and specified freight drivers; April restoration cargo-only. Official April 2 guidance specifically exempts humanitarian cargo at the China frontier.
events.imposing_authority: Kyrgyzstan government; bilateral implementation arrangements with China
events.enforcement: Formal government closure announcement; later Kyrgyz MFA cargo-restoration reports.
events.consequences: Not systematically assessed
events.relationship: Earlier China-specific frontier phase linked to national Kyrgyz regime CC011; neither independent national decision nor duplicate of March 19 foreign-entry ban.
events.status_observation: April 14 Irkeshtam freight restoration was agreed/reported; a May 22 ministry table counts resumed arrivals from April 16. June 8 Torugart freight restoration was only announced in the reviewed June 3 report. No full or first-passage reopening date is established.
events.official_rationale: Kyrgyz government cited preventing coronavirus entry.
events.context: Frontier-specific decision preceded Kyrgyzstan’s March national foreign-entry restriction.
events.uncertainty: Formal February 1 decision is not a claim of the first physical closure. Earlier January restriction and New Year shutdown overlap. Kabar and 24.kg rely on the same MFA lineage; April 14 is partial restoration, not complete frontier reopening. A May 22 ministry operational table counts resumed Irkeshtam arrivals from April 16; April 14 remains a diplomatic/reporting endpoint, not independently verified first vehicle passage.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope. No measured continuous interval is established.

events.title: Sarakhs Iran–Turkmenistan rail-freight COVID suspension
events.scope: Sarakhs international railway crossing
events.direction: Both directions
events.movement: Rail freight, including export and transit wagons
events.exceptions: No rail exception identified in reviewed accounts; no assertion about air or other routes.
events.imposing_authority: Government of Turkmenistan, according to Iranian officials
events.enforcement: Governor reports actual wagon movements; later customs statement corroborates resumption week.
events.consequences: Not systematically assessed
events.relationship: Additional rail mode distinct from CC014 foreign-road-truck/driver restrictions; grouped within Turkmen pandemic frontier regime.
events.status_observation: Rail wagons reported crossing both directions June 18, 2020.
events.official_rationale: Turkmen government sought to prevent coronavirus spread, according to its notification reported by Iranian officials.
events.context: Iran–Turkmen road restrictions followed a different timetable; May rail readiness and June road-bridge inauguration are not endpoints.
events.uncertainty: Exact onset unresolved within April 1–2: Iran Press governor accounts give April 2, whereas a contemporary IRICA table gives April 1 for goods transport at the frontier and a later nCa/IRICA republication also gives April 1 but mixes wagon/truck vocabulary. Direct Iran Press retrieval returned 502; substantive indexed articles were reviewed. June 18 wagon movements are corroborated by full-text Tehran Times/IRICA. Original Turkmen closure order not retrieved.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope. Do not compute a single-day duration until the April 1/April 2 onset discrepancy is reconciled. Closure is dated to April at present; competing days are retained in uncertainty. June 18 marks actual rail movement, not restoration of all road or passenger traffic.

Rail cargo only; road reopening and bridge ceremony are separate.

events.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
events.scope: Bilateral cargo clearance at Chi Ma–Ai Diem (Aidian)
events.direction: Both directions initially.
events.movement: Import/export freight through this gate.
events.exceptions: Restored trade was limited by commodity and transloading; this endpoint is first partial cargo movement.
events.imposing_authority: Chinese Ai Diem border authorities
events.enforcement: Gate interviews and provincial figures document actual resumed export/import vehicles.
events.relationship: Distinct from R6-EA-004 and R6-EA-005; December 22 traffic prevents a single continuous December–April spell.

events.uncertainty: December 22 marks partial trade restoration, not clearance of all stranded agricultural goods. A contemporaneous commander account gives mixed public-health and technical explanations; the evidence does not isolate each factor’s contribution.

events.exceptions: Essential purposes and commercial transport staff; from onset, non-commercial-vehicle entry by EU (including Latvian), EEA, Swiss and UK nationals, and EU permanent residents holding a Latvian residence permit, was not restricted under this provision.

events.uncertainty: June 16 is formal European-origin permission, not an observed first crossing. Unvaccinated entrants remained subject to testing/isolation; very-high-risk origin exceptions and intermediate amendments require separate treatment.
